territorial_scope.description: Applies across Canada and reaches foreign online undertakings that provide programming to Canadians.

evidence.quote: each foreign online undertaking shall make the greatest practicable use of Canadian creative and other human resources

summary.short: Amends the Broadcasting Act (assented 27 April 2023) to regulate online undertakings that transmit programs over the Internet: it adds them as a broadcasting class, exempts user-uploaded social media programs, and gives the CRTC order-making, expenditure and administrative penalty powers.
summary.long: The Act amends the Broadcasting Act to add online undertakings (transmitting programs over the Internet) as a distinct class of broadcasting undertakings. It excludes programs users upload to social media services, unless the provider uploads them or they are prescribed by regulation. It updates the broadcasting policy, including duties for foreign online undertakings to make the greatest practicable use of Canadian creative resources. The CRTC may make orders imposing conditions on broadcasting undertakings, such as Canadian programming proportions, carriage and information duties, and may require expenditures on Canadian programming. Licences remain required for non-online broadcasting undertakings; online undertakings need none. Offences carry fines, and administrative monetary penalties of up to $25,000 (individuals) or $10 million (other persons) for a first violation may be imposed, with a due diligence defence. Consequential amendments touch the Canada Elections Act, Copyright Act and Accessible Canada Act. Some provisions take effect on a date fixed by order; a parliamentary review follows in the fifth year.

notes: The document is the Act as enacted, not a consolidation of the amended Broadcasting Act. Section 54 is the only commencement provision in the text: it brings only subsections 40(2) to (4) into force by order; the text gives no commencement for the other provisions. Several amendments touch only one language version (e.g., section 10(1) French lead-in and section 10(2) English repeal), so the English and French texts are not parallel in places. Relations and entities target no registry IDs because none were supplied; target_instrument_id is left empty. Registry citation (S.C. 2023, c. 8) and the assent date are not in the operative text.
